actions.body: City of New Albany Community Development
actions.exact_result_status: City's current project-updates page lists multiple Meta new data-center/new-data-building projects at 1500 Beech Rd., 13385 Green Chapel Rd., and Clover Valley Rd. addresses, including active contractor listings for Turner Construction or Shive-Hattery. This supports site work-construction status for the New Albany Meta expansion footprint, but does not publish permit numbers, occupancy, energization, or MW by building.
actions.access_caveat: Snapshot date is the research access date, not a claimed permit-issue date.

actions.body: City of New Albany Community Development
actions.exact_result_status: December 2025 report lists Meta LCO 3, Meta NLH9S, Meta NLH1, Meta NLH2, Meta NLH3, Meta NLH5, Meta NLH100, Meta NLH6, Meta NAB1, Meta NAB2, Meta NAB9, Meta NAB3, Meta NAB5, Meta NAB100, and Meta NAH 9 with 2025 start dates; it also lists partial-occupancy status for Meta LCO DCB1 expiring March 29, 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Official monthly report supports active construction and one partial-occupancy entry, but does not prove Prometheus energization or full operation.

actions.exact_result_status: City statement says Meta's New Albany data center will draw power from the regional electric grid, that Meta pays the full cost of energy it uses, and that Meta's nuclear-energy agreements support operations including the Prometheus supercluster in the New Albany International Business Park; the city states no nuclear plant is planned in New Albany.
actions.access_caveat: Energy statement confirms Prometheus-New Albany linkage and power-cost position, not building completion.

actions.exact_result_status: Meta announced nuclear-energy projects supporting up to 6.6 GW of new and existing clean energy by 2035 and said the power will support grids serving Meta operations, including the Prometheus supercluster in New Albany, Ohio.
actions.access_caveat: Company energy announcement confirms Prometheus location and grid-support context; it does not provide a local permit, occupancy, or IT-load commissioning record.

actions.body: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg / Threads, corroborated by industry press
actions.action_type: company executive capacity and timing statement
actions.exact_result_status: Zuckerberg's Threads post, as quoted by multiple industry outlets, says SemiAnalysis reported Meta was on track for a 1 GW-plus supercluster; Zuckerberg said Meta is building several multi-GW clusters, calls the first Prometheus, and expects it online in 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Threads itself returned rate-limited during this refresh; capacity and timing are treated as reported/planned cluster scale, not verified metered load or live status.

actions.exact_result_status: Meta's New Albany campus page says Meta broke ground on the New Albany data center in 2017, has invested more than $1.5B in Ohio data centers, supports more than 300 operational jobs, and had 1,200 skilled trade workers on site at peak construction.
actions.access_caveat: Campus profile confirms owner/operator and legacy campus investment but does not isolate the Prometheus AI expansion capacity.

capacity_note: Reported/planned Prometheus supercluster scale is 1 GW-plus from Zuckerberg/SemiAnalysis coverage; city construction pages do not publish MW and no metered energization record was found. Treat 1000 MW as planned cluster scale, not verified live load.
